title: A self-tallying quantum anonymous voting protocol for multiple-selection elections
authors: Guang-Bao Xu, Meng-Na Li, Yu-Guang Yang, Dong-Huan Jiang
abstract: Self-tallying quantum anonymous voting (SQAV) has drawn considerable attention since it was proposed. However, constrained by design challenges, all existing protocols only accommodate single-selection voting and cannot support multi-selection voting. In this paper, we propose a SQAV protocol with multi-selection voting functionality. In our protocol, $nm$ $n$-particle entangled states are equally divided into $n$ groups, and the $n$ particles in each entangled state are delivered to $n$ voters, one particle per voter. Each voter obtains $n$ voting vectors by sequentially measuring all his (or her) particles that belong to $n$ different group, and then encodes his or her voting information into the vector corresponding to the secret index. Due to entanglement correlation, each voter can verify whether his or her ballot is correct through computation, while any participant can obtain the vote count for each candidate through computation. Our protocol satisfies self-tallying, nonreusability, verifiability, and fairness.
summary: This paper introduces a quantum cryptographic protocol for anonymous voting that extends previous work to support multiple-selection voting. It utilizes $n$-particle entangled states and complex measurement sequences in both computational and Fourier bases to ensure privacy and verifiable tallying. The resulting protocol satisfies key security properties like self-tallying and nonreusability.
main_problem: To develop a Self-tallying Quantum Anonymous Voting (SQAV) protocol that successfully supports multi-selection voting, overcoming the limitations of existing protocols restricted to single-selection voting.
main_result: The authors propose a novel SQAV protocol using $n$-particle entangled states that achieves multi-selection voting while maintaining self-tallying, nonreusability, verifiability, and fairness.
method: The protocol involves distributing entangled states, followed by sequential measurements in both computational and Fourier bases to generate secret indices and encode the multi-selection ballot vector.
model_or_system: The protocol is built upon $n$-particle entangled states, $|\Psi_nangle$, which are analyzed using properties derived from the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) in the context of quantum information theory.
key_observables: The total tally vector $ eta$ is the key observable, which allows any participant to calculate the count for each candidate. Verification involves checking $ eta(d_i) = v_i$.
important_parameters: The security parameter $\delta$ governs the probability of undetected eavesdropping, which decreases exponentially with $\delta$.
main_assumptions: The protocol assumes the existence of a trusted third party (T) for state preparation and distribution, and relies on pairwise authenticated classical channels.
paper_structure: The paper details the protocol in several steps: state preparation, eavesdropping detection using basis measurements, secret-index generation, and finally, the encoding and tallying of the multi-selection ballot vector using specific measurement correlations.
why_interesting: While focused on cryptography, the underlying resource—the manipulation and measurement of highly entangled quantum states—is a core topic in quantum information theory, relevant to quantum communication protocols.
